text:
Anna (product): Ok team — we need a concrete spec for the rerank endpoint to bring to PLG customers next quarter. main asks: flexible k behavior, predictable latency, and consistent scores across variants.

Mike (ml): Quick checklist: API shape, score normalization, truncation policy, precomputed embeddings, rollout/acceptance metrics. also a customer (GreenSearch) asked for percentile-based k (top 10%) not just absolute k.

Jordan (eng): Proposal draft for API shape (high level):
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "string",
  "candidates": [{"id":"string","text":"string","metadata":{}, "embedding": optional string}, ...],
  "k": 5,                     // or 0 for return all
  "k_mode": "absolute"|"percentile", // percentile accepts 0-100
  "score_mode": "raw"|"normalized", // server returns both if requested
  "normalize": "zscore"|"platt"|"softmax",
  "truncate_policy": {"per_candidate":"head"|"tail","max_tokens":512,"preserve_fields":["title"]}
}
```
Jordan (eng): Implementation notes: we should always return raw_score and normalized_score; keep raw for debugging. If percentile requested we compute k = max(1, ceil(n * pct/100)).

Sara (research): For normalization, platt scaling helps for probability-like outputs but needs calibration data per model. z-score is cheap and stable across batches — but not bounded. softmax gives bounded 0-1 but sensitive to temperature. Suggest default: return raw + zscore, and offer platt/softmax as opt-ins with calibration jobs.

Mike (ml): Agree. Also propose an option `pairwise_preference` toggle for customers who train with pairwise labels — we can return pairwise_score for ranking systems later. Not in MVP.

Leo (ops): Two operational constraints: 1) latency SLOs — p95 < 120ms for up to 20 candidates (hosted), 2) cost target — < $0.12 per 1k candidate-rows for standard small models. Truncation policy should default to per_candidate head trimming and global token cap to avoid OOM on bad payloads.

Anna (product): Launch acceptance criteria idea:
- Feature parity: absolute k + percentile k + return raw + normalized scores
- Metrics: MRR improvement >= 5% on benchmark prompt set, pairwise agreement >= 0.75 vs labeled set
- Performance: p95 latency < 120ms (<=20 cand), error rate < 0.5% on canary
- UX: clear error when k > candidates or invalid percentile request

Jordan (eng): Edge cases: ties and stable sort. We'll stable-sort by normalized_score, then fallback to candidate.id hash for deterministic tie-break. Also add `preserve_order` flag for customers who want input order respected when scores similar.

Sara (research): Truncation nuance: if a candidate has structured fields, we should preserve short fields (title, url) and truncate the long body. propose `preserve_fields` list in truncate_policy. Also call out precomputed embeddings: accept base64 or hex string and skip model encode step if present.

Mike (ml): Scoring normalization rollout: stage 1 (default zscore), stage 2 (offer platt via model-calibration job), stage 3 (allow customer-supplied normalization map). Need eval harness to detect regressions.

Anna (product): Prioritization — MVP scope for next release (90-day): absolute k, percentile k, raw+zscore, head truncation with preserve_fields, precomputed embeddings. Opt-ins (next 3 months): platt, softmax, pairwise.

Leo (ops): Canary plan: 1% traffic with synthetic and real workloads, monitor p95 latency, error rate, memory, and MRR on canary queries. rollback if error rate > 1% or p95 > 200ms.

Jordan (eng): Backend tasks: endpoint, parser, batching logic, truncate stage, normalize stage, metrics hooks. Estimate 3 sprint effort. Need a flaggable rollout and config per-customer (percentile allowed?).

Mike (ml): Evals to add: query-length sensitivity, candidate-length sensitivity, percentile vs absolute UX tests. Also add a short checklist for customers who supply embeddings: embedding-dim validation + checksum.

Anna (product): Customer negotiation notes: GreenSearch wants percentile + preserve context in body when truncating titles. agree MVP gives them percentile + preserve_fields. set expectation: platt calibration will come later.

Canary Bot: Canary deploy scheduled for 1769560000 for rerank/v2 to 1% traffic. Monitor tags: rerank_v2, canary, percentile_k

Anna (product): Action items: Jordan -> PR for API shape and server-side validation docs by EOD Wed. Mike -> eval harness (bench + labeled set) by next Tue. Leo -> canary playbook draft. Sara -> calibration plan for platt in a follow-up doc.

Jordan (eng): noted. I'll open the RFC and link in #product when ready.

Mike (ml): 👍

Sara (research): :thumbsup:

Leo (ops): ack.

Anna (product): thanks team — we'll sync on Wed to lock final acceptance criteria.
